notes: Hook overclaimed: "a rule for any temperature". The research says resistance depends on temperature only approximately linearly in many materials [R13], and the course brief treats extending copper's line far beyond the readings as a prediction, not a reading. Corrected to "a rule for other temperatures in that range" in topic.json.

oneBreath overclaimed: "A straight line on a graph has a rule, y = mx + c". A vertical line has an undefined gradient and the equation x = a [R3], and idea i3 says any line that is not vertical has y = mx + c. Corrected to "Any straight line on a graph that is not vertical has a rule, y = mx + c" in topic.json.

The rest checked against the research and lesson i1: gradient from two points [R1], m as the gradient [R2], c as the y-axis crossing [R8], two points or a point and a gradient fix the line [R9][R10], distance and midpoint [R4][R5][R6], and readings as a law with a resistor's ohms [R11][R12][R14]. "Roughly as a line" in the hook matches [R13]'s "approximately linear".
